scenes.heading: Creating a content approval workflow that doesn't slow you down

sents.d: Creating a content approval workflow that doesn't slow you down
Clear approval processes prevent both delays and unapproved posts going live.
Without a defined approval process, content either gets delayed waiting on scattered client feedback, or gets posted without proper sign-off, both of which create friction in the relationship.
A batch approval system — sending a full week or month of content at once for review, rather than post-by-post — is usually faster for both sides than a constant back-and-forth on individual posts.

Setting a default approval rule (e.g., if there's no response within 48 hours, content goes live as submitted) keeps the calendar moving even with a slow-to-respond client, as long as this rule is agreed to in advance.

take: Send content in batches with an agreed approval deadline.
